systems.name: Access-Controlled RAG on Databricks
systems.headline: Search proposes. Unity Catalog authorises.
systems.discoverySection: Plant the Hook in the Framing Sentence
systems.description: Keep the source design’s restricted base table and governed view separate, and re-read every candidate as the requesting user.
systems.question: A Tier-1 support agent asks why Vertex lost data and whether service credits apply.
systems.scope: This adapts the source’s two-layer Databricks design. It is a local explanation, not a workspace execution or a current-product deployment recipe.
systems.provenance: Adapted from the full canonical Databricks lesson. Table/view separation, filtered candidate search and governed user re-read are source-grounded. Payloads and failure outcomes are illustrative. Current official documentation was consulted for search governance constraints and terminology; source workspace measurements and OBO/reranker readiness are not reverified here.

discovery.question: Is Unity Catalog already the governance boundary?
discovery.answer: The source assumes a Unity Catalog metastore. Otherwise governance migration comes first.
discovery.decision: Make table privileges and the governed re-read a prerequisite, not a later retrofit.

discovery.question: Are account groups synced from the identity provider?
discovery.answer: The source expects SCIM-synced account groups.
discovery.decision: Test revocation propagation and token freshness; do not promise instantaneous identity-provider changes.

discovery.question: Must source permissions be mirrored per document?
discovery.answer: The source carries per-document tenant, sensitivity, region, compartment and validity rules.
discovery.decision: Compile a coarse index filter and enforce the full current policy at the governed read.

discovery.question: Is serverless available, and in which cloud and region?
discovery.answer: Availability and residency depend on the customer workspace. No workspace is selected for this explorer.
discovery.decision: Confirm SQL, inference and auth prerequisites in the intended region before implementation.

stages.title: Resolve the user inside the request
stages.what: A Tier-1 agent asks about Vertex. The handler obtains the caller’s forwarded credentials for this request, not a global client created at startup.
stages.why: The governed read must run as the user whose access is being decided.
stages.next: Next: Compile the first-layer filter.

input.question: Why did Vertex Financial lose data in March, and do they get service credits?

checks.text: No shared service-principal credential may stand in for the user at the governed read.

stages.title: Compile the first-layer filter
stages.what: The handler compiles tenant, clearance, region and permitted scalar group flags into the endpoint’s filter syntax. It carries the filter on every search.
stages.why: This reduces the candidate pool but is not the authoritative access decision.
stages.next: Next: Search the derived index for candidate IDs.

checks.text: Generate field names and values from trusted attributes and the known schema, not raw user text.

stages.title: Search the derived index for candidate IDs
stages.what: The serving identity runs filtered hybrid search. The example returns HELP-1 plus a stale TICKET-9 candidate. Index text is not used as answer context.
stages.why: A derived search index must not be assumed to inherit query-time table row filters or masks.
stages.next: Next: Enforce the principal’s current entitlement.

checks.text: Candidate IDs are proposals for a governed re-read, not permission to show index text.

stages.title: Re-read through the governed view as the user
stages.component: Governed SQL view + UC policy and masking
stages.what: The SQL read runs with the Tier-1 identity. Unity Catalog evaluates the policy, drops TICKET-9 and returns only HELP-1 with required PII masking.
stages.why: Only this governed result may reach the model; stale first-layer metadata cannot bypass it.
stages.next: Next: Answer only from the governed text.

checks.text: Apply tenant, clearance, residency, embargo, compartment, external and default-deny rules.
Use only the governed returned rows and masked content, never merge in raw index text.

stages.title: Answer only from the governed text
stages.what: The model explains the support-visible backlog and refers credit questions to the account manager. It cites HELP-1.
stages.why: A model should never have the contract or engineering post-mortem in this user’s context.
stages.next: Next: Verify the answer and trace the two layers.

output.answer: The support evidence describes a platform backlog. Ask the account manager about service credits.

checks.text: Assess grounding against the governed passage; no judge can grant extra access.

stages.title: Verify the answer and trace the two layers
stages.what: Verification checks the citation and claim support. The run trace records that TICKET-9 was proposed by search and dropped by governance; SQL access audit covers the governed read.
stages.why: The index candidate set and actual model context are different observability layers.
stages.next: Only governed, masked support evidence reaches the model. The stale search candidate is dropped and traced.

checks.text: Citation IDs must match permitted governed evidence.
Log search candidates separately; do not assume index access is a normal table-read audit event.

stages.component: Governed SQL view + Trace and audit
stages.what: The SQL warehouse or Unity Catalog dependency is unavailable. The handler records the failure and returns a refusal without using the index text.

scenarios.label: No usable forwarded user credential
scenarios.outcome: The request stops before search. A service-principal read cannot impersonate the user’s governance context.

stages.title: Reject a request without its user context
stages.what: The request has no usable forwarded user credential. The handler cannot perform the required governed read as that user, so it refuses before search.
stages.why: Caching a startup client or silently using a broader identity would invalidate layer 2.
stages.next: The request stops before search. A service-principal read cannot impersonate the user’s governance context.

checks.text: Do not fall back to a shared broad credential.

stages.title: Enforce the principal’s current entitlement
stages.component: Governed SQL view + UC policy and masking + Trace and audit
stages.what: The entitlement change is visible to the governed query, but the index is still stale. The governed view removes all proposed rows and the response refuses neutrally.
stages.why: Access changes should be checked at query time rather than waiting for re-embedding.
stages.next: The governed view returns no permitted rows for the changed principal. No answer is generated.

checks.text: This scenario assumes revocation has propagated to the query identity. Real propagation and token refresh must be tested.

scenarios.label: A human has access to the restricted base
scenarios.outcome: The privilege review fails. The design must not be released with a direct base-table bypass.

stages.title: Inspect the base-table grants
stages.what: A setup review finds a human principal with SELECT on the base table. That table is the sync source and does not carry the source design’s end-user enforcement.
stages.why: Protecting a view does not stop a user from reading a base table they can directly access.
stages.next: Next: Block the security gate until the grants are corrected.

checks.text: Only the trusted sync principal should read this base in the source design.

stages.title: Block the security gate until the grants are corrected
stages.component: Deterministic leak gate + Trace and audit
stages.what: The deterministic privilege check fails and records the unsafe grant. No claim of a secure deployment is made.
stages.why: This is a structural permission failure, not a low answer-quality score.
stages.next: The privilege review fails. The design must not be released with a direct base-table bypass.

checks.text: Retest with the affected human identity after correcting the grants.

scenarios.label: A forbidden document reaches actual model context
scenarios.outcome: The deterministic security assertion fails and blocks release. A high correctness score cannot override it.

stages.title: Evaluate the governed model-context IDs
stages.what: A deliberately bad test fixture puts a forbidden contract ID into the actual model context. The evaluator intersects forbidden IDs with the context IDs.
stages.why: Raw search overshoot is not a leak; forbidden text reaching the model is the event this test measures.
stages.next: Next: Record a blocked release.

checks.text: Use deterministic ID set arithmetic, not an LLM sufficiency judgement.

stages.title: Record a blocked release
stages.what: The release report records the failed security assertion. Quality and groundedness scores cannot make the gate pass.
stages.why: A leak is an incident-level boundary.
stages.next: The deterministic security assertion fails and blocks release. A high correctness score cannot override it.

checks.text: No positive judge score overrides a security failure.

scenarios.outcome: The sync principal feeds the derived index while end users receive only the governed view. This is a setup explanation, not a live provisioning run.

stages.title: Choose separate sync and governed read paths
stages.what: The source’s table-attached row-filter/mask setup cannot use that governed table directly as its index source. The design chooses a restricted base and a governed view.
stages.why: The source observed this constraint in its workspace; current policy types and exemptions must be checked before a real build.
stages.next: Next: Restrict the base and define the governed policy.

checks.text: The split must not create a human-readable ungoverned bypass.

stages.title: Restrict the base and define the governed policy
stages.component: Restricted base table + UC policy and masking
stages.what: The base is granted to the sync principal, while user reads use the policy-protected view. The view enforces current user attributes and masks PII.
stages.why: The two objects serve different identities and responsibilities.
stages.next: Next: Explain the derived index feed.

checks.text: Review grants on both objects and test with real personas.

stages.title: Explain the derived index feed
stages.what: Delta Sync derives the search index from the restricted base. Search results remain candidates requiring the governed user re-read.
stages.why: Index synchronisation does not prove end-user authorisation.
stages.next: The sync principal feeds the derived index while end users receive only the governed view. This is a setup explanation, not a live provisioning run.

revision.pitch: I would keep the two-layer access design, but make Unity Catalog the authority for the second layer. A derived search index is not a guarantee that table row filters and masks govern each search result. The source therefore separates a base table restricted to the sync identity from a governed view for users. At request time the handler resolves the user credential and compiles a coarse ACL filter for search. Search proposes chunk IDs. The handler then re-reads those IDs through the governed view as the requesting user. Only the allowed, masked text from that read reaches the model. If the credential, warehouse or governance layer is unavailable, we refuse instead of serving raw index text. I would test with real personas, inspect base-table grants and gate releases on deterministic checks of actual model-context IDs. Source workspace results and preview details are historical claims, not tests performed by this explorer.
revision.flow: Request user → compiled index filter → candidate IDs → governed re-read as user → masked permitted context → answer → verify and trace
requirements: Filtered hybrid candidate search, user-identity governed re-read, row/PII policy enforcement, grounded cited answers, query traces, separate index logging and deterministic security assertions.
No direct base-table bypass, tenant/residency boundaries, query-time authority, fail-closed governance and explicit workspace/auth prerequisites.
discovery: Is Unity Catalog already the governance boundary?
Are account groups synced from the identity provider?
Must source permissions be mirrored per document?
Is serverless available, and in which cloud and region?
revision.tradeoff: The extra governed read adds latency and an availability dependency, but keeps the authority at the enforcement engine rather than in the model or a search cache.
revision.failure: The index is available while the governed SQL read is down. Refuse; never route raw search text directly to the model.
ops: Use tenant boundaries appropriate to the customer and keep ACL updates separate from content re-embedding. Source endpoint capacity figures are not explorer benchmarks.
Measure search, SQL re-read and generation independently. Confirm auth propagation and token refresh in the intended workspace.
Provisioned endpoint/warehouse cost depends on utilisation; the source’s relative prices are not current quotes.
Test governed SQL as each persona, direct-base bypasses, masks, revocation and actual model-context IDs. Separate retrieved candidates from exposed evidence.
revision.remember: Only the governed user read supplies model context.
